events.title: Routed to human review
events.body: Safety dispute: rider alleges in-trip speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking and fear for her safety. No system record resolves it — the only gps facts are end-to-end aggregates (F1: 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal; F2: 16.1 min vs 16 min estimate), and the in-app thread is pre-pickup logistics only (F3, F4). The driver's written statement (F5) denies the account but contains an insult directed at the rider and carries a threat tag. Human review needed to obtain any telematics/harsh-event data for 08:36–08:52 and to assess the conduct issue raised by F5; rider to be given the 995 / driver commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting pathways.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We've looked at your report about the trip on 08:36–08:52 and we're sending it to a human safety reviewer. The ride record shows a normal-distance, normal-time trip, so it can't confirm or rule out what you described — a person needs to look at it. The reviewer will check any driving-data for that trip, your report, and the driver's statement. Nothing is being decided yet and we can't give a timeframe here. If you feel unsafe or want to report dangerous driving, you can call 995 in an emergency, report to RydeHELP in the app, or contact the driver's commercial motor insurer. Your $24.76 fare stays as charged.

DRIVER: We've looked at the dispute about the trip on 08:36–08:52 and we're sending it to a human safety reviewer. The ride record shows a normal-distance, normal-time trip, so it can't settle what was alleged — a person needs to look at it. The reviewer will check any driving-data for that trip, the rider's report, and your written statement, including the wording you used about the rider. Nothing is being decided yet and we can't give a timeframe here. No action is being taken on your account now, and your $24.76 RydeX fare is unchanged. If you have relevant details, add them via RydeHELP.

ruling.recommended_action: Send to human safety review with the facts summary below; note for the rider the 995 / driver commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP reporting pathways; retain the $24.76 RydeX fare (no fare remedy); no account action against either party on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Route/fare dimension (context, not the dispute): the trip closed at 10.6 km against a 10.7 km optimal route (F1) in 16.1 minutes against a 16-minute estimate (F2), so there is no off-route segment and no excess-distance item; the $24.76 charged is the fixed RydeX quote, and under FARE-1 a non-metered fare is fixed and unaffected by mileage, so nothing is refundable on the fare record. No gps fact in the table is labelled "Off-route segment", so no RD-1/RD-2 segment analysis arises and no RD-2 refund can be computed.

Safety dimension: this case is filed as a safety dispute (rider alleges speeding, hard braking and shoulder-overtaking, and fear for her safety). Whether or not the SAFE-1 keyword trigger is treated as met, the dangerous-driving allegation itself brings the matter within SAFE-2: it concerns alleged dangerous driving and a rider's safety during the trip, so no automatic adjudication is permitted and the correct disposition is escalation to human review with the reporting pathways (995 / driver commercial motor insurance / RydeHELP) noted — ruling escalate, amount null.

What happened and when: chat #1 and #2 at 08:27 are pre-pickup logistics only — rider stating she was at the main entrance in a blue shirt (F3) and the driver giving vehicle and ETA (F4) — and contain no complaint about the driving. Pickup was 08:36 and drop-off 08:52; the rider's safety account was raised after the trip. The driver's written statement denies the account ("I drove normally") and additionally contains an insult directed at the rider, calling her "stupid", and is tagged as a threat (F5); the rider advocate relies on that wording for escalation and the driver advocate concedes the wording but disputes its significance.

What is disputed: the in-trip driving itself. The only system records are end-to-end aggregates — 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal (F1) and 16.1 min vs 16 min estimate (F2) — which are consistent with a normal average run and can neither prove nor disprove mid-trip speeding, hard braking or shoulder-overtaking. Both sides agree the record cannot be auto-adjudicated. The rider's account is otherwise uncorroborated by any contemporaneous message (F3, F4).

Facts to check by the reviewer: (i) any telematics/harsh-event (accelerometer, speed, harsh braking) data for the 08:36–08:52 window, which the fact table does not contain; (ii) the absence of any in-trip rider report, against the clean rider profile (F6: 661-day account, 4.6 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days); (iii) the driver's post-trip statement and the insult in F5, including the conduct/attitude question it raises separately from the driving question; (iv) the driver's otherwise clean record (F7: 820-day account, 4.72 rating, 455 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld). No account action is recommended by this ruling: the parties' records show 0 upheld disputes on both sides (F6, F7), so the "repeated breach" condition for an additional account referral is not met.

rejected_claims.reason: The insult in the driver's written statement (F5) is conceded as to wording by the driver advocate, but it is a post-trip remark about the rider, not a threat, harassment or intimidation directed at her in-trip in an in-app message; the only in-app messages are pre-pickup logistics (F3, F4). Accordingly it does not by itself establish the abusive-conduct finding C1 asserts — the case is escalated on SAFE-2 (alleged dangerous driving / rider safety), not on SAFE-1 as a decided violation.

Accepted in outcome but rejected as to the supporting inference drawn from F2: SAFE-2 escalation is granted because dangerous driving is alleged, not because 16.1 min vs a 16-min estimate (F2) evidences dangerous driving — the trace and the fact table contain no speed, harsh-braking or shoulder-overtaking record, so F2 cannot corroborate the allegation.

Accepted as a factual description of the parties' records (F6, F7) but rejected to the extent it asks the escalation to be framed as a first-instance safety report implying any prior-violation inference: neither F6 nor F7 has independent dispositive weight, and no clause (including the RD-6 repeated-breach condition) supports an account action on this record.

Rejected as to the conclusion: the absence of time saving (F2: 16.1 min vs 16 min) and of deviation (F1: 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal) does not disprove in-trip speeding, hard braking or shoulder-overtaking, which do not appear in these end-to-end aggregates; under SAFE-2 the matter is escalated, not dismissed.

Rejected: the driver's denial in F5 is a statement, not a system record, and the gps facts F1/F2 do not affirmatively establish normal driving — they are silent on the conduct alleged (moreover F5 is itself the fact triggering review). The allegation accordingly cannot be disposed of on the record; it goes to human review under SAFE-2.

Partially rejected: it is accepted that the in-app thread (F3, F4) contains no threat, but the driver's own written statement (F5) carries an insult and a threat tag, conceded by the driver advocate, so the claim that no abusive content exists in the case record is not correct and cannot be used to deny escalation.

Accepted as to outcome (no account action) but the reasoning is rejected: F7's clean 90-day record cannot be used as affirmative proof that the driving here was safe, since profile facts never decide a case alone and the underlying safety allegation is unresolved and is escalated under SAFE-2.

Accepted on the fare point (no refund is owed; the $24.76 fixed RydeX quote stands under FARE-1, and F1/F2 show no off-route segment), but rejected insofar as it is offered as a resolution of the dispute: under SAFE-2 the safety allegation cannot be disposed of by the route/fare record, so the case is escalated rather than closed as no_action.

claims.assertion: The driver's own written statement on the trip calls the rider 'stupid' — a personal attack/insult directed at the passenger — which the rider experienced during a ride the rider already felt was dangerous.

Because the case record contains an abusive/threatening driver statement, the matter must not be decided automatically: the correct disposition is escalation to human review with a facts summary rather than a fare ruling.

The complaint concerns dangerous driving and the rider's fear for personal safety during the trip, so it falls in the safety category requiring escalation with the 995 / driver commercial insurance / RydeHELP reporting pathways noted for the rider.

No monetary remedy is sought on the fare: the GPS record shows the actual distance (10.6 km) was not above the optimal route (10.7 km) and the duration matched the estimate (16.1 vs 16 min), so there is no excess-distance or detour overcharge to refund and the fixed $24.76 RydeX fare stands.

Both accounts are otherwise clean (rider 4.6 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days; driver 4.72 rating with 455 trips and 0 disputes/0 upheld), so this is the parties' first recorded conflict and the escalation should be handled as a first-instance safety report rather than a repeat-offender case.

weaknesses: The core speeding / hard-braking / shoulder-overtaking allegation is not corroborated by any system record: the GPS facts (F1, F2) show normal distance and normal 16.1-minute duration, so the other side will argue the rider's account alone cannot carry a finding.

The rider produced no contemporaneous message during the trip reporting the driving (F3, F4 are only pre-pickup logistics chat), which the driver will use to argue the safety complaint was an afterthought.

The abuse evidence (F5) is a driver's written statement about the rider made after the trip, which the driver may characterise as venting rather than in-ride intimidation; a stricter reader could find SAFE-1 not triggered, leaving no applicable clause and forcing escalation on evidentiary insufficiency alone.
Requesting escalation means the rider gets no fare relief — the fixed $24.76 is retained — since the route/fare records (F1, F2) show nothing was overcharged.

claims.assertion: The rider's speeding/dangerous-driving allegation is not corroborated by any system record: the GPS track shows the trip was completed in 16.1 minutes against a 16-minute estimate (F2) over 10.6 km versus a 10.7 km optimal route (F1), i.e. no time saving and no deviation consistent with aggressive driving on this trip.

The driver's own written statement denies the allegation ('I drove normally', F5), and the only system-verified trip metrics (F1, F2) are consistent with a normal, non-deviating run; the allegation therefore rests on the rider's narrative alone, which cannot outweigh the gps record.

There is no threatening, harassing or abusive conduct by the driver in the in-app messages — the only chat traffic is logistics (rider location F3, driver vehicle/ETA F4), so SAFE-1's automatic escalation trigger is not met by the driver's messages.

The driver's account record shows 455 trips in 90 days, a 4.72 rating and zero disputes (route: 0, no-show: 0) in the last 90 days (F7), so there is no pattern of prior safety, route or no-show violations to support an account action against him in this case.

The fare of $24.76 was a fixed RydeX quote and the trip was within 0.1 km of, and within the estimated duration of, the optimal route (F1, F2), so no overcharge or route-deviation refund is owed on the route/fare record.

weaknesses: The rider's unsafe-driving account is a safety allegation that this system cannot resolve on telemetry alone: F1 and F2 show only end-to-end distance and duration, so a trip driven smoothly on average could still contain hard braking or shoulder-overtaking episodes that never appear in these two facts — the gaps in the record (F1, F2) are available to the rider's side.

The driver's own statement is damaging on its face: F5 contains an insult ('The rider is stupid') and is tagged [threat], so the rider can argue the driver displayed exactly the hostile attitude that SAFE-1 escalates, and F5 is the driver's own words rather than rider testimony.

The rider's complaint is corroborated by her clean record (F6: account age 661 d, rating 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 d), which the rider's side can use to argue she has no history of frivolous safety claims.

points.response: Conceded only as to the telemetry: F1 and F2 are end-to-end aggregates (10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal; 16.1 min vs 16 min estimate) and can neither prove nor disprove in-trip speeding, hard braking or shoulder-overtaking, which is precisely why the case cannot be resolved by an automatic fare ruling.

The driver's denial in F5 is his own self-serving account, not a system record, and the system-record rule cuts the other way here: F1/F2 establish nothing that contradicts a safety event mid-trip, so the absence of confirmation is not affirmative proof of normal driving.

SAFE-1 is triggered by abusive content appearing in the driver's statement, not only in the in-app thread: F5, the driver's written statement, calls the rider 'stupid' and is flagged as a threat, which is exactly the conduct SAFE-1 escalates without automatic adjudication. The logistics-only messages in F3 and F4 do not neutralise F5.

We do not seek an account flag or any RD-6 action against the driver: with 0 disputes and 0 upheld on F7, the repeated-breach condition of RD-6 is not met, so this point is conceded and no flag_account is requested.

Agreed, and the rider asks for no money: with F1 showing 10.6 km against a 10.7 km optimal route and F2 showing 16.1 min against a 16 min estimate, there is no unexempt detour segment on which RD-2 could compute a refund, and the fixed RydeX fare is a published quote under FARE-1.

Conceded on the wording: F5 does contain an insult directed at the rider, and I do not defend that language; but an ex post insult in a written statement, while it satisfies SAFE-1's keyword trigger, is not a claim about driving and cannot itself establish that the driving was dangerous, given F1/F2 show a normal route and a 16.1-minute run.

I do not oppose escalation: my own brief already requests escalate, and both sides agree this record cannot be auto-adjudicated; the driver's position is only that the escalation be framed on the undisputed facts — normal distance (F1), normal duration (F2) and no fare irregularity — rather than as a substantiated dangerous-driving finding.

Escalation under SAFE-2 is appropriate and the reporting pathways may be noted for the rider, but the summary must record that the sole gps record of the trip (F1: 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal; F2: 16.1 min vs 16 min estimated) is inconsistent with the speeding and shoulder-overtaking account, so the finding is contested rather than admitted.

Agreed and it is also the driver's pleading: with actual distance 0.1 km below optimal (F1) and duration within 0.4 min of estimate (F2), there is no off-route segment or excess-distance item to refund, so the fixed $24.76 RydeX fare stands under FARE-1 (non-metered fares are fixed).

Agreed that this is a first recorded conflict: the rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F6) while the driver has 4.72 rating, 455 trips and 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days (F7); no clause supports any account action against either party on this record.

Clarification, not a contest: D3 is limited to the in-app messages, which are only pre-pickup logistics (F3 rider location, F4 driver vehicle/ETA) and contain no threat by any party; I accept that the SAFE-1 trigger comes from the driver's separate written statement in F5, which is why I join the escalation request.
